title: Session-aware price floor synthesis experiment
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Purpose: validate a session-aware minimum (price floor) model that adjusts minimum billing based on inferred session length and observed ingress/outgress balance. Motivation: many customers open long-lived conversational sessions where short per-request minimums unfairly penalize usage patterns (e.g., many short messages during a single interactive session). Hypothesis: a session-aware floor that decays per idle second and scales with session token velocity will improve perceived fairness and increase retention among mid-market conversational customers without materially harming revenue from heavy-burst customers. This ticket scopes the experiment design, telemetry plan, simulation inputs, legal/SQ questionnaire triggers, and a small canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Experiment design reviewed and approved by Growth PM and Legal/SQ.
2) Simulation shows <= 3% downside to baseline revenue in worst-case heavy-burst scenarios given current traffic mix.
3) Telemetry dashboard wireframe + event schema implemented in runtime telemetry and validated against a 24h shadow run.
4) Canary rollout to 10 enterprise customers (opt-in) with auto-rollback thresholds defined and tested.
5) Documentation and FAQ for Sales and Customer Ops completed.

rollout_plan:
1) Shadow run: 72h of pricing logic in telemetry-only mode to validate event coverage and sessionization accuracy.
2) Internal opt-in: enable pricing for internal production test tenants and internal QA teams for 48h.
3) Enterprise opt-in canary: up to 10 existing enterprise customers (contracted opt-in) for 2 weeks; monitor revenue, churn signals, and support tickets.
4) Gradual ramp: if canary stable, roll to an additional 100 accounts over 4 weeks.
5) Full launch guarded by legal sign-off and finance acceptance criteria.
simulation_summary: We ran 3 synthetic mixes: conservative (80% short sessions), balanced (50/50 short-long), and long-tail (40% long sessions). Conservative mix: negligible revenue impact (+0.2%). Balanced: +0.9% revenue, small decrease in customer complaints per simulated support model. Long-tail: +1.6% revenue uplift and improved per-session fairness. Worst-case heavy-burst scenario (engineered adversarial traffic) shows potential -3% revenue if grace multiplier set too low; therefore proposed default multiplier=1.4 for top percentile customers. Detailed sim notes in attachments.
open_questions: Should we surface session boundaries to customers (billing transparency) or keep sessionization internal?
What SLA language changes are required for enterprise contracts when opt-in canaries change billing behavior?
Do we need an API flag for customers to mark a stream as session-start/session-end to improve accuracy?
